x: Derrick Burfitt, the holder, Vernon Blowfield, who won in 1947, and Tom Carter, who scored wins in 1938, 1939 and then again when the race was resumed in 1945, were all absentees on this occasion, but even so, the field included two British Olympic representatives in Bill Lucas and Jack Braughton.
Two British Olympic runners in Bill Lucas and Jack Braughton were among the starters and although they both beat 9.50 they found they could not overtake the leaders.

Len Herbert and Jack Braughton, both International runners, came in together for fourth place, and then came Les Stokell ninth, with John Bromley, running his first race for us since he became qualified, in tenth position, and we had the spectacle of four Belgraves fighting for the honour to be our…

Len Herbert was 52nd, Jack Braughton 75th and Ted Stimpson 79th, and to finish in the first 100 in this event is quite good running. There was a field of over 200 with 27 counties from all over England being represented and once again the Northern runners demonstrated their superiority with Lancashi…

Our team was minus Len Herbert and Len Adams, not to mention Jack Braughton and Jimmy Wood, who are eligible for this event, so that although we were pressed rather closely by Herne Hill Harriers, who had Greene, of Reading, assisting them, we can be quite satisfied with the actual result.
Walker, ran a fine race to retain his hold on the Shield although Jack Braughton gave him a close race, and a good sign was the fact that our first six men were all home within 42 seconds.

Walker just beat Eddie Short for second place, and then came Jack Braughton 5th, Bill Lucas 7th, Archie Bedford 9th and Len Herbert 11th. All the first five were selected to run for Surrey in the Inter-Counties race at York, and Jack Brown 7th in the Kent race and A.
Pirie and also running in their team were J. Braughton 29th, Bill Lucas 44th, Eddie Short 53rd, Chas.
The 2 miles run saw Jack Braughton, another 2nd claim member, turning out and from the virtual scratch mark he went through his field to win easily in good time.

Walker brought us to 5th on the third leg, and we then ran Jack Braughton in an endeavour to overhaul the leaders. Jack ran a fine lap in 14.7 which was only 5 seconds outside the course record set up by C.

We were not at full strength owing to the absence of Jack Braughton, Len Herbert, Archie Bedford and Len Adams, and did not expect to retain our team title, which we had held for the past two seasons.
Jim Masters was our first man home and deservedly gained his County Colours by finishing fourth. Our other scorers were J.

At this stage another second claim member, Jack Braughton, was just ahead of a large group of runners checked in at 29m.10s. which included Eric Gebbett, Len Adams, Ken Stimpson, Bert Jordan, and about another dozen runner.

As I have said the race started in perfect weather and at 3½ miles things had sorted themselves out with a leading group of 12, then Colin 14th and another group of 12 or so led by our second claim member Jack Braughton, with Eric 24th.

Walker, Jack Braughton, and Archie Bedford were among the non-starters and of those who were running only two were in full training. Half way round the first lap, Bagnall, Paterson, Short, Masters and Baulch were all between 20th and 30th in that order and Gebbett and Trower were in the next dozen.
J. Braughton, a second claim member was 6th.
Also taking part was Jack Braughton who has now become a first claim member. He will prove very valuable when he gets back to his normal form.

Several Belgravians can be found amongst the many photographs including Jack Braughton (2nd claim), Charlie Walker, John Bromley, Bill Nankeville, Peter Bagnall, Tom Morrell, Len Herbert, John Davies, Mike Shingles, Charlie Dabbs and Gerry North.

Other members of the British team had been Belgravians during the war including Doug Wilson, Rene Howell and Jack Braughton. Among the visiting teams Canada had a Belgravian as team manager but the Belgian marathon bronze medallist Etienne Gailly became one of the heroes of 1948.
